title: 4D Chicago Scene
description: A scene names a date and a terrain epoch. Everything else in the dataset resolves against it. Adding a year is a new scene file, not a restructure.

target_date.description: The single date this scene depicts. Enforced against every structure phase.

terrain_epoch.description: Must resolve in data/terrain/epochs.json, and its interval must cover target_date.

terrain_apron.description: T-2502. Optional: an apron field beside the terrain box, as <epoch>/<file>.json under data/terrain/epochs/ - a second heightfield the renderer samples outside the box before its fallback, drawn in place of the box's carried apron over the field's cut_local_enu_m. 1812's carries the ground down the South Branch to Lee's Place.

lighting.description: A specific, documented moment — not a vibe. Sun azimuth and elevation are computed from this plus the datum lat/lon.

anchors.description: Named viewpoints. The smoke harness reads the same anchors the walkthrough uses, so screenshots and gameplay can never diverge.

altitude_m.description: Metres above local ground. Present = this is an AERIAL viewpoint: arriving at it puts the visitor in free-fly at this height rather than on foot. Absent = a standing viewpoint, which is the historical default and stays so.

pitch_deg.description: Look angle, negative is downward. Only meaningful alongside altitude_m — a standing viewpoint looks at the horizon.

layers.description: What the renderer mounts for this scene (T-1739), and nothing it does not list. `terrain` and `water` are the epoch's own ground and water. `structures` is the structure records that resolve at target_date. The rest are the town's derived and authored layers, every one of them written for 1 July 1835 in a directory that carries no date: `flora` (the sward, the timber and the ground's substrate colours), `fauna`, `streets`, `enclosures` (with the ground inside them), `signage`, `yard_goods`, `frontage`, `wharves`, `boats`, `wells`, `residents` (the people directory), `businesses` (the firms register) and `exclusions` (the research record of buildings left out, and the watch list); tools/compile_scene.py compiles the people directory and the exclusions record only for a scene that lists them. The drawer follows the same list (T-1740): `residents` offers the People section and the City, Population and Order book topics, `businesses` the Firms section, `fauna` the wildlife topic, `flora` the plants topic and `exclusions` the not-here and open-questions topics, and a scene that does not list one offers none of what it carries. `street_grid` is a dated layer, data/street_grid/<scene>.json (T-0474, the 1904 Prairie Avenue carriageways, block faces, alleys and parcels). `context` is the faded context city (T-2477): data/context/<scene>.json, generated by tools/build_context_1904.py, simple stand-ins read off the Sanborn sheets and projected past them on every part of the map not yet built. `street_trees` is data/street_trees/<scene>.json (T-2473, the parkway elms planted on that grid's parkway bands). `street_furniture` is data/street_furniture/<scene>.json (T-3199, the gas lamps on that grid's parkways, generated by tools/lay_prairie_1904_street_furniture.py). `railway` is a dated layer, data/railway/<scene>.json (T-2478, the 1904 Illinois Central tracks along the lake, their ballast, ties and verges). `humans` is the human figures (T-1788): data/humans/instances/<scene>/index.json and the instance records it names, each bound to a person in that scene's people directory and drawn only as data/humans/contract.json § l1 allows — while L1 is in force, nobody. A scene of another date lists only what is true of it. `standing_horses` is a scene-scoped reconstructed development animal layer from data/transport/parked/standing-horses.json; one licensed canonical26 planted-standing clip, no walking, hitching or riding qualification.

released.description: Cannot be true while any included structure carries review_required.

cards.description: Interpretive cards the welcome panel opens for this scene (T-0472): what an event is called, what the evidence for it is and whose it is, where the accounts disagree, and what the scene deliberately does not show. The card's `text` is this project's own prose; every `quotes` entry is a source's words, verbatim, with the locator it was read at, and its source_id must resolve in data/sources. A card that quotes carries a confidence (documented needs a quote; inferred and conjectural need a confidence_note). A card with no quote is `kind: project` - a statement of what this reconstruction does, which claims nothing about the past. `review_required` here blocks the scene from release exactly as it does on a structure, and the card must say why in its own `review_note` (tools/validate.py, the AGENTS.md standing constraint).

cite.description: The attribution the visitor reads under the quote: whose words, and where printed. The locator is for the next reader of the data; this is for the person on the card.

static_support_regions.description: Optional small scene-authored static support rectangle for an explicitly drawn standing-horse layer. yards.js snapshots only the actual yard base triangles overlapping this region BEFORE normal coarse upload release; the original town CPU geometry still releases. Current renderer independently caps one region,4square metres,32triangles and4096typed-array bytes, with owned disposal; a missing/oversized support cache refuses the horse. Not a collision surface or historical surveying claim.
